title: Construction of a machine learning-based risk prediction model for acute stroke in maintenance hemodialysis patients
summary: A model developed from 1,100 maintenance-hemodialysis patients predicted acute stroke in a held-out 330-patient test set. XGBoost achieved AUC 0.847 (95% CI 0.791–0.902), sensitivity 0.73 and specificity 0.83. The study is single-center and retrospective; external validation and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning algorithms; XGBoost performed best
organization: Department of Nursing; Kidney Disease Center, The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: A single-center retrospective dataset of 1,100 patients was split into 770 training and 330 test cases. XGBoost achieved test AUC 0.847 (95% CI 0.791–0.902), sensitivity 0.73 and specificity 0.83.
evidence.unknown: The study reports no external validation or clinical-impact evaluation; performance beyond this held-out single-center cohort is unknown.
evidence.ai_role: Seven machine-learning algorithms were trained on clinical variables to estimate acute-stroke risk in maintenance-hemodialysis patients; XGBoost was the best-performing model.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
